messages:
maya: heads-up — since kernel-selection v2.4 rolled ~30m ago we see a ~12% drop in prefix cache hit-rate and a steady GPU memory increase on prod (started ~6m ago). attaching profiler links and a quick flame. anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: thanks — is this correlated with the batching heuristic flip (max-batch->adaptive) we enabled yesterday? could be different request shapes hitting new kernel paths. link to batch metrics: https://grafana/redwood/prod/batches

olga: quick profiler dump: KV cache churn is through the roof. lots of tiny keys (median key ~56 bytes) and high LRU churn; hit-rate falls for medium-length prompts. also see a spike in CPU->GPU memcpy freq. pasted histogram:```
key_size_bytes: 10, 50, 100, 200
hit_rate_by_key_size: 0.12, 0.45, 0.28, 0.52
LRU_evictions_per_min: 1200
fragmentation_estimate: 0.37
```

kevin: hypothesis: kernel-selector is choosing a new fast path that changes tokenization/prefix normalization (or changes how we compute cache keys for aligned kv-sharding). result: more distinct keys (lower key re-use) -> warmup penalty -> higher memcpy and OOM risk.

maya: do we have a diff of cache key serialization between stable and v2.4? could be subtle hash salt or prefix trimming change.

olga: dug into the commit: we switched from canonicalized prefix trimming to an trimmed+suffix-preserve mode for perf; that reduces average key length but increases key cardinality for similar logical prefixes. attaching snippet:```
// old: canonicalize(prefix) -> hash
// new: trimSuffixKeepBoundary(prefix) -> hash
```

sam: that matches. more distinct keys -> lower hit-rate. mitigation options: 1) revert keying change (risky), 2) cohort TTL smoothing (keep recently-seen similar prefixes alive longer), 3) prefill hot cohorts during warmup, 4) size-aware eviction to avoid fragmenting GPU slabs.

kevin: propose experiment: implement TTL smoothing by cohort (cohort = prefix length bucket + first-token hash mod 16). algorithm: when eviction would remove an item in a "hot" cohort (recent RPS above threshold), extend TTL by 2x and move to MRU position. cheap to implement in runtime. config patch:```json
{"eviction_policy":"size_aware_lru_cohort","ttl_smoothing_factors":{"small":1.0,"medium":2.0,"large":1.5},"cohort_buckets":16}
```

maya: risk = if cohorting keeps many medium-size keys around we could blow GPU memory. what's the safe guard?

olga: add soft-evict watermark at 78% GPU cache usage that switches to strict size-aware eviction and refuses prefill. also adjust slab allocation to reduce fragmentation: increase min-slab to 4KB and prefer 64B coalescing. these two knobs kept a similar incident from tripping OOM in staging.

sam: plan for canary: roll TTL-smoothing on 10% traffic, monitor: prefix_hit_rate, eviction_rate, GPU_cache_util, memcpy_ops/s, p95 latency. abort if GPU_cache_util > 85% or eviction_rate > 2x baseline.

ops-bot: deploy request received: "prefix-cohort-ttl-smoothing" -> canary 10% traffic -> start at 1859994400.

kevin: i'll push the patch to canary branch now (PR #4387). includes metrics exports + guard rails. will also add a debug flag to revert to old keying without restart.

maya: thanks. olga, can you precompute a hot-cohort list from last 24h to prefill the canary nodes on boot? aim for top 2k keys, only keys > 48 bytes and hit-rate > 0.6.

olga: yep, will run a one-off job to generate prefill snapshot and upload to s3://redwood-cache-prefill/canary-1859994321.tar.gz. job start ~1859994470.

kevin: note: we'll also add a short-term metric 'cache_key_entropy' to detect sudden increases in key cardinality — if entropy rises > 20% we auto-toggle to size-aware fallback.

maya: timeline: canary today, measure for 30m, then 50% if green, full rollout tomorrow morning. keep the rollback quick.

sam: also record whether the kernel path selection histogram correlates with requests that have new keying — if so we may need to pin kernel-selection for some model families.

olga: started prefill job, ETA ~3m. posting logs: "prefill 0/2100... done 2100/2100, size 34MB" :thumbsup:

ops-bot: canary started at 1859994400 on cluster rwd-canary-7 (10% traffic). monitoring hooks active.

maya: thanks everyone. keep updates short in this thread. if we see OOM signs, revert keying -> rollback v2.4 and stop canary.

kevin: ping me if canary shows >10% latency regression for p95; i'll disable ttl-smoothing immediately.

sam: copying notes into runbook and incident channel. good luck.

maya: closing loop later with postmortem if rollout changes root cause. appreciate the quick triage. :heart:
